title: 2020 AMC 10B Problem 21
statement: In square \(ABCD,\) points \(E\) and \(H\) lie on \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{DA},\) respectively, so that \(AE=AH.\) Points \(F\) and \(G\) lie on \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{CD},\) respectively, and points \(I\) and \(J\) lie on \(\overline{EH}\) so that \(\overline{FI} \perp \overline{EH}\) and \(\overline{GJ} \perp \overline{EH}.\) See the figure below. Triangle \(AEH,\) quadrilateral \(BFIE,\) quadrilateral \(DHJG,\) and pentagon \(FCGJI\) each has area \(1.\) What is \(FI^2?\)

solutions.text:
The four named regions fill the square and each has area \(1,\) so the square has area \(4\) and side length \(2.\) Since triangle \(AEH\) is right isosceles with area \(1,\) we have \(AE=AH=\sqrt2.\)

Extend \(FI\) to meet \(AB\) at \(K,\) and set \(x=BF\) and \(t=BE=2-\sqrt2.\) Because \(EH\) has slope \(-1,\) line \(FK\) has slope \(1,\) so \(BF=BK=x.\) If \(K\) were on segment \(EB,\) then region \(BFIE\) would lie inside triangle \(BFK,\) whose area would be at most \(\frac{t^2}{2}<1,\) a contradiction. Thus \(K\) lies to the left of \(E,\) and \(EK=x-t.\)

Triangle \(BFK\) is right isosceles with area \(\frac{x^2}{2}.\) Triangle \(EIK\) is right isosceles with hypotenuse \(EK=x-t,\) so its area is \(\frac{(x-t)^2}{4}.\) Since their difference is region \(BFIE,\) \[1=\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{(x-t)^2}{4}.\] Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} 4&=2x^2-(x-t)^2\\ &=(x+t)^2-2t^2. \end{aligned} \]

Also, \(FK=x\sqrt2\) and \(KI=\frac{x-t}{\sqrt2},\) so \[FI=FK-KI=\frac{x+t}{\sqrt2}.\] It follows that \[ \begin{aligned} FI^2&=\frac{(x+t)^2}{2}\\ &=2+t^2\\ &=2+(2-\sqrt2)^2\\ &=8-4\sqrt2. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B .
